rationale: Branch-vs-base review of 18 files (production change confined to session-signals.ts, claude-named-invocations.ts, their tests, and the OTLP architecture doc; the rest of the diff is this branch's own already-approved sdlc-light run artifacts from a prior review round — plan.md, qa-report.md, decisions.jsonl, code-review-final.json/code-review-check.json, etc.). Blind, edge-case, and acceptance lenses all ran with parseable output; acceptance ran against the two Jira tickets' acceptance criteria (EPMCDME-15582, EPMCDME-17201). All of EPMCDME-15582's ACs and the client-observable half of EPMCDME-17201's ACs (AC4/AC5; AC1-3 are backend/UI, out of scope for this diff) pass against the provided unit tests. One new blocking finding (CR-001): the blind lens and edge-case lens independently flagged that `nextSkillName`'s lookahead (the EPMCDME-17201 dedup fix) gives up after inspecting exactly one assistant-role message, and I confirmed this against this repo's own real transcript fixture (tests/integration/session/fixtures/session-3fe1b6bc.jsonl, lines 227-229): a single logical assistant turn is commonly split into multiple consecutive JSONL lines sharing one message id (a `thinking`-only line, then a `text`-only line, then the line actually carrying the `Skill` tool_use) — `nextSkillName` inspects only the first of these (the `thinking` line), finds no `Skill` block in it, and returns `''` immediately without looking at the next two lines that are where the real tool_use lives. This means the EPMCDME-17201 dedup silently fails to fire on this common real-world transcript shape (not a rare corner case — it is the shape of the one Skill-tool_use example present in this repo's own fixtures), reproducing the exact double-count bug the fix exists to prevent, in a shape none of the new unit tests exercise (they only test a direct-adjacency case and a single isMeta bookkeeping line, never a multi-part assistant turn). Five other observations raised by the lenses were triaged as non-blocking and are not emitted as findings: (1) `matchCommandNames`/`recordCommand` reuse the same `fromIndex` for every command tag found in one message, so a message with two command wrappers can only have one deduped against the following Skill call — plausible but very low real-world frequency (a single user message rarely carries two distinct command invocations) and untested; (2) `nextSkillName` returns only the first `Skill` tool_use in its candidate message, so a message with two sequential Skill calls could misclassify the second — same low-frequency profile; (3) `wrappedCommandName` returns only the first `<command-name>` match in a line, documented as intentional; (4) `LOCAL_ONLY_COMMANDS` has no automated cross-repo sync check against the backend's `SENTINEL_EXACT` list — already an explicit, user-approved, documented tradeoff carried over from the prior review round; (5) the acceptance lens noted that suppressing a skill-backed command from `commandsInOrder` could change `session-summary.ts`'s `primary_command` (`commandsInOrder[0]`) when the first command of a session is skill-backed — a plausible side effect with no stated AC and no test, worth a follow-up test but not blocking since the field's new value (the skill name takes its place, since it's still the first *named thing* if nothing else precedes it) is arguably more correct, not less. All three standards checks (commit format, code quality, security) pass: all 5 commits on this branch follow Conventional Commits; no `any`/unsafe types introduced; no secrets, injection, or unsafe I/O in the pure in-memory diff.

findings.title: Skill lookahead gives up after one assistant-role message
findings.problem: nextSkillName(fromIndex) skips isMeta/isSidechain lines, then inspects exactly ONE subsequent message: if its role is 'assistant' but that specific message's content has no Skill tool_use, the function returns '' immediately instead of continuing to look at the next assistant-role message. A single logical assistant turn is commonly split into several consecutive JSONL lines sharing one message id (verified in this repo's own fixture tests/integration/session/fixtures/session-3fe1b6bc.jsonl lines 227-229: a 'thinking'-only line, then a 'text'-only line, then the line that actually carries the Skill tool_use) — none of this diff's new tests construct that shape; they only cover direct adjacency and a single isMeta bookkeeping line.
findings.impact: On this common real transcript shape, a skill-backed slash command is still double-counted as both a command and a skill — the exact EPMCDME-17201 bug this diff exists to fix reappears for any session where the model emits thinking/text before the Skill tool_use as separate transcript lines, which per the repo's own fixtures is normal, not rare.
findings.recommendation: Widen nextSkillName to keep scanning forward across consecutive assistant-role messages that share the same assistant turn (e.g. continue past an assistant-role message with no matching tool_use as long as content contains no non-tool_use terminal signal, or simply continue until a non-assistant-role message or a Skill tool_use is found, bounded by a small max-lookahead) instead of returning '' on the first assistant-role message that doesn't itself contain the Skill call. Add a regression test using a thinking-only + text-only + tool_use sequence shaped like the real fixture.
